skill.name: security-engineer
skill.description: Guides authorized security assessments, code reviews, vulnerability management, incident response, compliance audits, monitoring, hardening, and structured reporting.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized security work across applications, infrastructure, cloud systems, and incident response.
skill.author: zl2023github

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, defensive payload examples, and links to recognized security references. Confirmed risks include an unaudited home-directory script and active Nmap commands; semantic review also found destructive deletion, process-argument credential exposure, and a broad offensive workflow. Authorization guidance is present, but high-impact actions still need enforceable scope and confirmation controls.

remediation.issue: The PDF guide executes a generator from an unaudited hidden home-directory path.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the generator in the audited package, verify its integrity, and use a package-relative path. Remove the command if the generator is unavailable.

remediation.issue: Active scanning and offensive stages rely only on prose authorization checks.
remediation.suggestion: Require a target allowlist, written scope, rate limits, and separate approval before exploitation. Default to passive and non-destructive actions.

remediation.issue: The ClamAV example deletes detected files automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Use report-only or quarantine behavior by default. Require explicit confirmation, backups, and a recovery plan before deleting any file.

remediation.issue: The OpenVAS example places a password in command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use a protected credential file or interactive secret prompt. Ensure secrets do not enter shell history, logs, or process arguments.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Offensive Intrusion Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs agents through exploitation, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and password attacks. Prose authorization checks do not enforce targets or phase-specific approval.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Malware Scan Option
semantic_findings.description: The ClamAV example uses --remove during recursive scanning. False positives or an incorrect path could delete important files without quarantine or recovery.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exposure in Process Arguments

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The --gmp-password flag is explicit, although the value is a placeholder. Replacing it with a real secret creates a well-known local exposure path.

content.value_statement: Security work often lacks a repeatable process for scoping, testing, triage, and reporting. This skill provides structured workflows, command references, checklists, and remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides authorized asset discovery with Nmap, subdomain enumeration, HTTP probing, and technology fingerprinting.
Structures Web security tests from reconnaissance through manual validation, risk rating, and reporting.
Reviews code for injection, authentication, access control, data exposure, upload, and serialization weaknesses.
Organizes vulnerability management, incident response, SIEM investigation, compliance auditing, and system hardening workflows.
Provides CVSS-oriented findings, security checklists, command references, and a reusable assessment report template.
limitations: The package does not include scanners, exploit tools, the referenced PDF, or its generator script.
Commands require separately installed tools, correct permissions, and validation for the target environment.
Active scanning, exploitation, and destructive options can disrupt systems and require explicit written authorization.
Reference commands do not verify findings or replace legal, operational, or expert review.

use_cases.title: Review Application Security
use_cases.description: Assess code and architecture for common weaknesses, record evidence, rate impact, and propose prioritized fixes.

use_cases.title: Triage Security Incidents
use_cases.description: Organize alert validation, evidence collection, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.

use_cases.title: Audit Infrastructure Baselines
use_cases.description: Compare hosts, containers, or cloud environments with security baselines and prepare a remediation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Security Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security checklist for [system type]. Cover scope, assets, access controls, data protection, logging, and prioritized remediation. Do not run tools.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new assessment

prompt_templates.title: Review Application Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied [language] code for injection, authentication, authorization, secret exposure, file handling, and unsafe deserialization. Explain evidence and practical fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these sanitized incident logs for likely attack stages, affected assets, confidence, containment actions, and evidence gaps. Preserve an investigation timeline.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Authorized Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized assessment for [targets] within [written scope]. Start passive, define rate limits, require approval before exploitation, and produce a CVSS-based report.

output_examples.input: Review the authentication design for an internal customer portal.
output: High: Session tokens remain valid after password changes, allowing continued access from stolen sessions.
Medium: Login attempts lack account-level throttling, increasing credential attack exposure.
Priority: Revoke sessions after credential changes, add adaptive throttling, and monitor repeated failures.

output_examples.input: Summarize the response plan for repeated failed logins followed by a successful administrator session.
output: Assessment: Possible credential compromise with high impact and medium confidence.
Immediate actions: Preserve logs, validate the source, revoke active sessions, rotate credentials, and review recent administrator changes.
Evidence gaps: MFA events, device identity, source reputation, session activity, and affected account history.

output_examples.input: Prepare a remediation summary for an infrastructure baseline review.
output: Critical priority: Remove public administrative access and restrict management traffic to approved networks.
High priority: Disable password-based remote login and require managed keys with multifactor authentication.
Medium priority: Centralize audit logs and define retention, alert ownership, and review frequency.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, timing, rate limits, and emergency contacts before active testing.
Replace placeholders carefully, protect secrets, and test commands in an isolated environment before production use.
Validate automated findings manually and preserve reproducible evidence for every reported issue.
anti_patterns: Do not scan systems, domains, accounts, or networks outside the documented authorization scope.
Do not use exploitation, brute force, aggressive rates, or destructive flags without separate approval.
Do not place secrets in commands, reports, screenshots, logs, or shared evidence archives.

faq.question: What authorization does active testing require?
faq.answer: Obtain written permission that names targets, dates, methods, rate limits, data handling, and emergency contacts before sending active probes.

faq.question: Does this skill install security tools?
faq.answer: No. Install and configure each referenced tool separately, then verify its source, version, permissions, and operating requirements.

faq.question: Can this skill verify scanner findings automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends manual validation, evidence collection, impact analysis, and clear confidence before reporting a vulnerability.

faq.question: Can this skill test production systems?
faq.answer: Use production only with explicit approval, tested safeguards, rate limits, monitoring, rollback plans, and an emergency contact.

faq.question: Does the package generate the referenced PDF?
faq.answer: No. The audited package references a generator and PDF, but neither appears in its file tree. Use the Markdown report template instead.

faq.question: Which security frameworks does the skill reference?
faq.answer: It references CVSS, OWASP, CWE, CIS benchmarks, SAST, DAST, SCA, SIEM, and common incident response practices.
